title: Choosing a thinning method
text: zhang_suen default. lee 2-D adaptation Lee’s original 3-D algorithm. 3-D case (volumetric thinning) implemented release. hilditch method implements parallel form commonly cited “Hilditch” modern image-processing surveys; Hilditch’s 1969 paper actually describes sequential algorithm within-pass deletion tracking different crossing-number definition. See Lam, Lee & Suen (1992) relationship two. K3M lookup tables A_0 … A_5 reproduced Saeed et al. (2010), Section 3.3, page 327. OPTA’s safe-point boolean expression Holt’s condition H taken original papers; Lam-Lee-Suen 1992 survey used cross-reference one transcription error Holt’s middle clause (north vs east) corrected original.

title: Choosing a thinning method
text: thinning algorithms produce broadly similar skeletons V — collapse two diagonal strokes single lines meet bottom. Differences show complex shapes: zhang_suen aggressive simple shapes. guo_hall k3m preserve corners marginally better. hilditch look-ahead crossing-number check, gives different connectivity properties junctions. holt uses edge information neighbouring pixels rather crossing-number check central pixel; specifically designed preserve 2-pixel-wide lines.

title: Choosing a thinning method
text: zhang_suen — default. predictable behavior. Use general purpose thinning. guo_hall — try skeletons lots diagonal features Zhang-Suen breaking corners. lee — want directional processing (four sub-iterations per pass, one per cardinal direction). Sometimes produces cleaner skeletons asymmetric inputs. k3m — strongest corner preservation published comparative studies, cost slower (six phases per outer iteration vs. two Zhang-Suen). hilditch — well-cited historical algorithm; look-ahead crossing-number check makes connectivity slightly different parallel algorithms. opta — one-pass safe-point algorithm. N2 condition protects two-4-adjacent-pixel diagonal patterns, can leave stray pixels bar corners (documented property SPTA). holt — 2-pixel-wide lines preserved. algorithm uses edge information neighbouring pixels 5x5 window, allowing single subcycle.

text: simple bench::mark() comparison moderate image (illustrative): thinning algorithms O(iterations × pixels). Constant factors smallest zhang_suen guo_hall; holt k3m expensive look-aheads. what: 1. Edge handling: shapes that touch the frame
title: Correctness properties: edge handling, connectivity, and boundary cases
text: Every kernel reads 8-neighbourhood, border pixel neighbours lie outside matrix. simplest implementation — iterate interior pixels 2..(n-1) — never even considers border pixel deletion. shape touches frame keeps two- three-pixel-thick ridge along edge, silently violating one-pixel-wide contract entire point thinning. papers intend frame armour object: written shape drawn unbounded background. thinr reproduces surrounding image one-pixel background margin thinning cropping back afterward, shape skeletonised identically whether touches border. thinning removes pixels, image supplied one-pixel background margin must come back margin still clear — property cheap assert every method:
code: # A 3-pixel-thick horizontal bar flush against the top edge. bar_top <- matrix(0L, nrow = 5, ncol = 9) bar_top[1:3, ] <- 1L  # The same bar one row in from the edge. bar_interior <- matrix(0L, nrow = 5, ncol = 9) bar_interior[2:4, ] <- 1L  # Both thin to a single-pixel line, and to the same number of pixels. sum(thin(bar_top)) #> [1] 6 sum(thin(bar_interior)) #> [1] 6 methods <- c("zhang_suen", "guo_hall", "lee", "k3m",              "hilditch", "opta", "holt") vapply(methods, function(m) {   out <- thin(bar_top, method = m)   # No foreground survives more than one pixel thick on the top edge.   max(colSums(out[1:2, , drop = FALSE])) <= 1L }, logical(1)) #> zhang_suen   guo_hall        lee        k3m   hilditch       opta       holt  #>       TRUE       TRUE       TRUE       TRUE       TRUE       TRUE       TRUE

what: 2. Connectivity: thin strokes must not fragment
title: Correctness properties: edge handling, connectivity, and boundary cases
text: thinning pass may delete many pixels, must delete many connected object falls apart. classic failure two-pixel-wide stroke: edges stroke judged deletable pre-pass snapshot removed together, middle vanishes stroke collapses disconnected fragments. parallel algorithms avoid sub-iterations (Zhang–Suen Guo–Hall alternate two passes complementary conditions), sequential algorithms avoid making deletion visible opposing side tested. OPTA/SPTA sequential case: Naccache & Shinghal’s formulation performs two raster scans per cycle precisely removing one side stroke seen side considered. implementation instead evaluates four contour directions one frozen snapshot deletes single batch faster write published algorithm — fragments exactly two-pixel strokes method designed preserve. thinr’s guarantee one methods provide: object starts single 8-connected component thins single 8-connected component. two-pixel-wide bar thins connected one-pixel line. Every method returns 1: stroke stays connected. (guarantee enforced, OPTA returned four corner pixels bar — four disconnected components — good example locally-valid, globally-broken skeleton.)
code: # 8-connected component count. n_components <- function(m) {   m <- m != 0   lab <- matrix(0L, nrow(m), ncol(m))   k <- 0L   for (i in seq_len(nrow(m))) for (j in seq_len(ncol(m))) {     if (m[i, j] && lab[i, j] == 0L) {       k <- k + 1L       stack <- list(c(i, j))       lab[i, j] <- k       while (length(stack)) {         p <- stack[[length(stack)]]         stack[[length(stack)]] <- NULL         for (di in -1:1) for (dj in -1:1) {           r <- p[1] + di           cc <- p[2] + dj           if (r >= 1 && r <= nrow(m) && cc >= 1 && cc <= ncol(m) &&                 m[r, cc] && lab[r, cc] == 0L) {             lab[r, cc] <- k             stack[[length(stack) + 1]] <- c(r, cc)           }         }       }     }   }   k }  # A 2-pixel-thick, 9-pixel-long bar: one component in, one component out. bar2 <- matrix(0L, nrow = 6, ncol = 13) bar2[3:4, 3:11] <- 1L vapply(methods, function(m) n_components(thin(bar2, method = m)),        integer(1)) #> zhang_suen   guo_hall        lee        k3m   hilditch       opta       holt  #>          1          1          1          1          1          1          1

Often better corner preservation diagonal features. lee — Lee, Kashyap & Chu (1994) doi:10.1006/cgip.1994.1042 , 2-D adaptation. Four directional sub-iterations. k3m — Saeed, Tabędzki, Rybnik & Adamski (2010) doi:10.2478/v10006-010-0024-4 . Six-phase lookup-table thinning. hilditch — parallel form commonly attributed Hilditch (1969, Machine Intelligence 4). Single-pass thinning look-ahead crossing-number check. opta — Naccache & Shinghal (1984), "investigation skeletonization approach Hilditch", Pattern Recognition 17(3):279-284. One-pass safe-point thinning (SPTA). holt — Holt, Stewart, Clint & Perrott (1987) doi:10.1145/12527.12531 . One-subcycle parallel thinning edge information neighbours. See thin() vignette("choosing--method") guidance.

title: thinr: Binary Image Thinning Algorithms — thinr-package
text: medial_axis() — Medial axis transform (Blum 1967): locus foreground pixels ridge points distance transform. Optionally returns per-pixel distance. distance_transform() — Euclidean (Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher 2012, linear-time separable), Manhattan, Chessboard distance foreground pixel nearest background pixel.

title: thinr: Binary Image Thinning Algorithms — thinr-package
text: EBImage, dominant image-processing package R/Bioconductor, supplies binary morphology (dilate(), erode(), distmap(), watershed()) thinning / skeletonization operator. thinr fills gap small, dependency-light, LGPL-3 package (licence EBImage).

title: thinr (development version)
text: Correctness fixes figureextract ecosystem review (2026-07-03). boundary conditions published algorithms assume away; see new vignette("correctness-properties") guarantees restore. thin() now skeletonises shapes touch matrix border correctly. kernels inspect 8-neighbourhood never deleted pixels outermost row column, leaving edge-touching shapes two three pixels thick; thin() now pads image one-pixel background margin crops back, shape thins identically whether touches frame. Applies seven methods (#F012). thin(method = "opta") now keeps two-pixel-wide strokes connected. SPTA kernel evaluated four contour directions pre-cycle snapshot deleted one batch, sides 2px stroke removed together skeleton fragmented (2×9 bar collapsed four corner pixels). Deletion now sequential per direction, Naccache & Shinghal’s two-scan formulation requires (#F011). distance_transform(metric = "manhattan" | "chessboard") now returns Inf fully-foreground image (background pixel exists), matching "euclidean" metric EBImage::distmap(). two-pass metrics previously seeded foreground finite sentinel leaked plausible-looking meaningless finite distance (#F015). thin(), distance_transform(), medial_axis() now reject NA input clear error coercion boundary instead silently turning NA_integer_ (INT_MIN) C++ kernels (#F016). Added connectivity-preservation property test across seven methods tightened Holt straight-line test (#F013). Removed thinImage(). Use thin() (Zhang-Suen default method).
